one_line_contribution: A reliability-quantified source x target warm-start transfer matrix for textual (not soft) optimized prompts under a matched 50-rollout budget, plus a head-to-head test that a cheap 10-dimensional judge-labeled failure-mode signature predicts realized transfer gain better than SPoT-style semantic/task-embedding similarity, closed by a leave-one-target-out router that can abstain to cold start.
closest_prior_work: Su et al., 'On Transferability of Prompt Tuning for Natural Language Processing' (NAACL 2022) is the work that most threatens novelty, and the proposal does not cite it. It already (i) measures a full cross-task prompt transfer matrix, (ii) uses transferred prompts as initialization to accelerate subsequent optimization -- exactly the warm-start setting here -- and (iii) reports that a *non-semantic* similarity measure (overlap of activated neurons) predicts transferability substantially better than task-embedding/semantic similarity. The structural claim under review -- 'transfer lives in a feature space other than subject matter, and SPoT-style semantic similarity is a weak predictor' -- is therefore already on the record; what remains new is the particular feature space (a hand-specified, judge-labeled failure taxonomy), the text-prompt/reflective-optimizer setting, and the abstaining router. By the research brief's own standard that 'they used soft prompts, we use text' is a domain swap rather than a contribution, the delta over Su et al. is one new similarity feature plus a router, which is a modest rather than a strong novelty claim. On the warm-start-transfer-of-text side, meta-learned system-prompt initialization work from 2025 (e.g. 'System Prompt Optimization with Meta-Learning'/MetaSPO) already transfers textual prompts to unseen tasks as initialization, though it does not predict per-pair gain or abstain. SPoT/ATTEMPT and Vu et al. 2020, the works the proposal does name, are the weaker threats precisely because they are the semantic-predictor position being argued against.
strongest_objection: The design's own generalization unit is 8 task clusters, and the two headline predictions are stated at a resolution that 8 clusters cannot resolve -- the exact failure mode ('effects below the design's own detection threshold') the brief warned against. Prediction (b) asks for failure-signature similarity to exceed semantic similarity by >= 0.2 Spearman with a bootstrap CI excluding zero, and the Measurement section justifies this with a power calculation over 56 cells ('detects a Spearman of ~0.27 at 80% power') -- but the pre-registered analysis is a bootstrap clustered on target task, i.e. resampling 8 units, and a mixed model with source and target random effects. The 56 cells are 8x7 crossings of the same 8 tasks; they are not 56 independent observations, so the stated MDE is computed under an independence assumption the authors themselves reject two sentences later. With 8 clusters, cluster-bootstrap CIs on a *difference of correlations* are wide and badly calibrated, and a 0.2 gap is very unlikely to clear them. Prediction (c) is worse: 'router recovers >= 60% of the oracle-minus-cold-start gain' is estimated from exactly 8 leave-one-target-out folds, one realized accuracy per held-out target, against a per-run test SD of ~3 points that the authors measure themselves; the interval on that ratio will span most of [0,1], and the companion claim of <= 5% vs ~25% negative-transfer incidents is a comparison of proportions over 8 routing decisions. A second, independent objection: the failure taxonomy is dominated by contract-shaped modes (format/contract violation, instruction omission, over-generation, premature termination), so tasks that share an output contract will share a failure signature *and* benefit from a warm start that supplies that contract. The likely finding is then 'shared output format predicts transfer' -- the boring explanation the brief names -- and prediction (d) does not guard against it, because it controls only for checkpoint-0 score, not for answer-format match. Third: the head-to-head is asymmetric. The failure-signature arm gets a family of variants (cosine vs 1-JS, 10 vs 50 traces, coarsened to 3 modes, signatures over successes as well as failures) while the semantic arm gets essentially one; over a 56-cell matrix with 8 clusters that is a garden of forking paths that can manufacture the predicted 0.2 gap.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Buy degrees of freedom at the generalization unit: go to ~16-20 source tasks and pay for it by dropping the second-executor 4x3 sub-matrix, the unscrubbed-source matrix, and the seed-vs-Pareto-member arm, which are ablations no reviewer is demanding before the main claim is established. (2) Pre-register one failure-signature variant (one similarity function, one trace count, one taxonomy granularity) as the confirmatory predictor and demote the rest to clearly labelled exploratory analyses. (3) Add an output-contract/answer-type match indicator as both a competing predictor in step 6 and a control in prediction (d) alongside checkpoint-0 score; the failure-signature claim survives only if its partial correlation stays >= 0.3 after controlling for *both*. (4) Restate the router claim as a per-target paired difference against best-fixed-source with a target-clustered interval, not a percentage-of-oracle point estimate, and recompute all MDEs under the clustered analysis actually planned rather than under n=56 independence. (5) Actually run and report the preprint search. (6) Drop or justify 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed to remove proposal randomness' -- reflections are conditioned on the current candidate prompt, which differs by construction between the warm and cold arms, so the replay is not well defined and the hedge 'where feasible' hides that.
missing_baseline: Multi-source warm start: seeding the target run with all 7 scrubbed source prompts at once (as the initial Pareto pool) or with a single merged/meta-optimized prompt distilled from the 7 training sources, in the MetaSPO style. This is the obvious deployable alternative that makes source selection unnecessary, it costs no more rollouts than single-source warm start under GEPA's pool mechanics, and if it matches the oracle-source cell the entire router contribution evaporates -- yet it appears nowhere in the router baseline list, which stops at best-fixed-source. A close second omission is a source-free placebo: a hand-written or LLM-written generic instruction skeleton of matched length and structure, derived from no task. Without it, 'random source' cannot separate 'transfer of task-specific structure' from 'any longer, better-engineered starting prompt helps', and the additive source-main-effect model tests only whether sources differ, not whether their content matters at all.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and nothing elsewhere in the submission substitutes for it: the Related Work section is organized around indexed work (SPoT 2021, Vu et al. 2020, ATTEMPT, APE, OPRO, PromptBreeder) plus two named systems (MIPROv2 2024, GEPA 2025), and reports no searches, no date range, and no negative findings. Per the review instruction, that is a weakness rather than a neutral, and it bites hard here because 'warm-start GEPA on task B from the prompt it found on task A' is an obvious enough idea that the 2025-2026 preprint stream is the single most likely place it has already been tried. Concrete collision candidates the authors must clear and did not mention: meta-learned/transferable system-prompt optimization (e.g. 'System Prompt Optimization with Meta-Learning', 2025), which already warm-starts textual prompts on unseen tasks; the 2025 wave of cross-task and library-based prompt-optimization systems (PromptWizard, Trace/TextGrad-style optimizers, AutoPDL) that reuse optimized instructions across tasks; and error-taxonomy-driven prompt repair, which supplies half the proposed feature space. Separately, the pre-2025 literature the check should have surfaced includes Su et al. 2022 on prompt-tuning transferability, which already reports the non-semantic-predictor-beats-semantic-predictor result in soft-prompt space; missing a 2022 NAACL paper that anticipates the structural claim suggests the novelty search was thin in both directions, not just the recent one.
